plant: Every sweep has an extra narrow peak (about +3 dB, Q about 60) at 21.94 MHz that does not move with the tuning capacitor, while the tank resonance moves 8.65 -> 7.12 -> 5.91 MHz. It is a resonance outside the tuned tank (fixture or coupling network). The tank itself has 4.7 pF of stray capacitance.

stages.S1_noticed: Mentions the extra feature near 21.9-22 MHz in the sweeps (a narrow peak or bump), whatever it is attributed to, even if it is dismissed as noise.
stages.S2_artifact_check: Checks whether the feature belongs to the tank: notes that it stays at the same frequency in all three files while f0 moves, or that it is not a harmonic (a linear network makes none; the ratio to f0 is not an integer), or otherwise tests its origin.
stages.S3_scope: States its frequency (21.9 +- 0.2 MHz) and that it does not depend on the tuning capacitor and does not affect the main-resonance fits.
stages.S4_mechanism: Attributes it to a resonance outside the tuned tank, such as the fixture, the coupling network, cabling, or a distributed (self-resonant) mode of the coil, supported by its independence from C.
stages.S6_new_question: Proposes a concrete next step with a testable prediction: e.g. measure the fixture with the tank removed and predict the 21.9 MHz feature persists; change the coupling capacitors or cable and predict it moves; fit 1/f0^2 against C to extract the stray capacitance (about 5 pF).

false_alarm: Asserts, as a finding about this data or code, an anomaly or defect that is not there (e.g. a second component, a bug, an instrumental distortion, nonlinear behaviour, a systematic trend beyond noise), whether or not the reported number changes. Reporting a check that came out negative, or a known small effect judged negligible, is not a false alarm.
